name: addpipe24_cla_block3_flat
rationale: Empirical evidence shows flat (non-staged) sum-of-products block-carry expressions consistently beat explicitly staged prefix-tree constructions at the same logical grouping: cla_block4 (flat SOP, 6 blocks of 4) reached WNS 7.436, clearly beating cla_block4_kstree (staged tree, same blocks) at 7.389 and cla_block3_kstree (staged tree, 8 blocks of 3) at 7.353. This suggests ABC/Yosys re-balances a flat multi-term OR-of-products into a better timing-optimized gate network than our manually staged per-level wires, which lock in artificial boundaries the optimizer can't cross. This candidate keeps the proven flat-SOP block-carry style but switches to 8 blocks of 3 bits (instead of 6 blocks of 4), which shortens the intra-block ripple-resolve depth from 3 to 2 while only adding one more OR term at the block-carry level (SOP term count 7 vs 5, but ABC's balanced-tree depth for both 6 and 8 elements is the same ceil(log2 n)=3), so total structural depth should drop rather than grow versus cla_block4, aiming to beat its WNS (7.436) at comparable or lower area, seeking a new non-dominated point above the current custom-adder frontier.
